speaker: Teacher (union announced)
question: What is announced?
premises: athocyate samastānāṃ śāstrāṇāmiha melanam — now the union of all scriptures is told: the śāstramelana charter.
iha tāvatsama sto 'yaṃ vyavahāraḥ purātanaḥ — here, for now, the whole ancient practice stands (print crux kept, flagged).
inference: Charter: the ancient whole practice; its scriptures' union.
uncertainties: tāvatsama sto'yaṃ print crux — kept as-is, flagged.

speaker: Teacher (prasiddhi as āgama)
question: What grounds scripture?
premises: prasiddhimanusandhāya saiva cāgama ucyate — having sought prasiddhi: that very certainty is āgama.
anvayavyatirekau hi prasiddherupajīvakau — for conjunction and exclusion depend on prasiddhi.
inference: Prasiddhi grounds both scripture and reasoning.

speaker: Teacher (self-grounding fails)
question: Can manifestations self-ground?
premises: svāyattatve tayorvyaktipūge kiṃ syāttayorgatiḥ — in dependence-on-self, what would be the course of the two's manifestation-groups?
pratyakṣamapi netrātmadīpārthādiviśeṣajam — even perception, born of eye-self-lamp-object specifics: instruments need a ground.
inference: Self-grounding fails; even perception needs prasiddhi beneath it.

speaker: Teacher (hungry child)
question: Who needs given certainty?
premises: apekṣate tatra mūle prasiddhiṃ tāṃ tathātmikām — it requires, at the root, that thus-natured prasiddhi.
abhitaḥsaṃvṛte jāta ekākī kṣudhitaḥ śiśuḥ — born wrapped all around, one, alone, hungry: a child.
inference: The child-thought-experiment: a lone hungry beginning needs given certainty.

speaker: Teacher (act-questions)
question: What does the child lack?
premises: kiṃ karotu kimādattāṃ kena paśyatu kiṃ vrajet — what should he do, take, see by, approach?
nanu vastuśatākīrṇe sthāne 'pyasya yadeva hi — indeed, even in a hundred-strewn place, whatever for him: no principle without prasiddhi.
inference: Without given certainty every act-question stalls.

speaker: Teacher (serenity decides)
question: How does the child proceed?
premises: paśyato jighrato vāpi spṛśataḥ saṃprasīdati — of one seeing, smelling, touching: consciousness is serene.
cetastadevādāya drāk so 'nvayavyatirekabhāk — taking that very principle at once, it bears conjunction-exclusion.
inference: Serene consciousness takes the principle at once; anvaya-vyatireka follows.

speaker: Teacher (shaped serenity)
question: Is serene consciousness unshaped?
premises: hanta cetaḥprasādo 'pi yo 'sāvarthaviśeṣagaḥ — well! even the serene consciousness, whatever goes with specific meaning.
so 'pi prāgvāsanārūpavimarśaparikalpitaḥ — it too is previously fashioned by vāsanā-shaped reflection.
inference: Even serenity is vāsanā-shaped: no groundless beginning.

speaker: Teacher (neither outer proof nor flash)
question: What is prasiddhi not?
premises: na pratyakṣānumānādibāhyamānaprasādajaḥ — not born of perception-inference-etc-outer-proof-serenity.
prāgvāsanopajīvyetat pratibhāmātrameva na — dependent-on-vāsanā previously, this mere intuition is not.
inference: Neither outer-proof product nor bare flash: vāsanā-fed prasiddhi.

speaker: Teacher (mud-test)
question: Why no mud-eating?
premises: na mṛdabhyavahārecchā puṃso bālasya jāyate — no desire for eating-mud of a man, a child's, arises.
prāgvāsanopajīvī cedvimarśaḥ sā ca vāsanā — if reflection feeds on prior vāsanā — and she is vāsanā.
inference: Vāsanā explains restraint: the past works in the present.

speaker: Teacher (former-time prasiddhi)
question: Where does prasiddhi come from?
premises: prācyā cedāgatā seyaṃ prasiddhiḥ paurvakālikī — if come from the east, that — this prasiddhi — of former time.
naca cetaḥprasattyaiva sarvo vyavahṛtikramaḥ — and not by consciousness-serenity alone runs the whole sequence of practice.
inference: Former-time prasiddhi; serenity alone doesn't run practice.

speaker: Teacher (root accepted)
question: What ends the regress?
premises: mūlaṃ prasiddhistanmānaṃ sarvatraiveti gṛhyatām — root: prasiddhi — that is proof: 'everywhere indeed' accept.
pūrvapūrvopajīvitvamārgaṇe sā kvacitsvayam — in seeking dependence-of-the-prior, she herself somewhere stands.
inference: Accept prasiddhi as root-proof; regress ends in her.

speaker: Teacher (doubtless shining)
question: Where did practice shine?
premises: sarvajñarūpe hyekasminniḥśaṅkaṃ bhāsata purā — for in that one all-knowing-nature, without doubt it shone before.
vyavahāro hi naikatra samastaḥ ko 'pi mātari — for practice is nowhere entire in a proof.
inference: Practice shone doubtless in the all-knowing one; no single proof holds it all.

speaker: Teacher (numbers don't prove)
question: Do many knowers prove?
premises: tenāsarvajñapūrvatvamātreṇaiṣā na siddhyati — hence by mere non-all-knowing-priority this is not established.
bahusarvajñapūrvatve na mānaṃ cāsti kiṃcana — in many-all-knowing-priorities no proof at all exists.
inference: Neither few nor many prior knowers prove anything.

speaker: Teacher (Bhairava as certainty)
question: Who is certainty?
premises: bhogāpavargataddhetuprasiddhiśataśobhitaḥ — gleaming with a hundred certainties of pleasure-release-and-their-causes.
tadvimarśasvabhāvo 'sau bhairavaḥ parameśvaraḥ — of that reflection-nature is he: Bhairava, the Supreme Lord.
inference: Certainty personified: Bhairava gleaming with a hundred prasiddhis.

speaker: Teacher (descent into world)
question: How does certainty reach practice?
premises: tataścāṃśāṃśikāyogātsā — then too, from part-part union: she.
prasiddhiḥ paramparām śāstraṃ vāśritya vitatā lokānsaṃvyavahārayet — prasiddhi, having resorted to tradition or scripture, spread, should make worlds practice.
inference: Certainty descends part-by-part through tradition into world-practice.

speaker: Teacher (all co-depend)
question: On what do all co-depend?
premises: tayaivāśaiśavātsarve vyavahāradharājuṣaḥ santaḥ samupajīvanti — by that very childhood all practice-bearers co-depend.
śaivamevādyamāgamam — on the Śaiva indeed, the first āgama.
inference: All practice co-depends on the first Śaiva āgama.

speaker: Teacher (partial sharers)
question: Who shares partially?
premises: apūrṇāstu pare tena na mokṣaphalabhāginaḥ — but the incomplete others: hence not liberation-fruit shareholders.
yāvattu tāvattatphalabhāginaḥ — as far as — but that far shareholders of that fruit.
inference: Incomplete followers share fruit only so far as they follow.

speaker: Teacher (eating refutes pramāṇas)
question: What proves eating?
premises: bālyāpāye 'pi yadbhoktumannameṣa pravartate — even at childhood's end, whatever to-eat is set going.
tatprasiddhyaiva nādhyakṣānnānumānādasambhavāt — by that certainty alone: not perception, inference, or impossibility.
inference: Eating runs on certainty, refuting the pramāṇas.

speaker: Teacher (word-understanding ends doubt)
question: What stills doubt?
premises: naca kāpyatra doṣāśaṅkāyāśca nivṛttitaḥ — and nowhere here does fault-hope-doubt cease by itself.
prasiddhiścāvigānotthā pratītiḥ śabdanātmikā — but prasiddhi-born-of-non-cognition: understanding, word-natured.
inference: Word-natured understanding from non-cognitive prasiddhi stills doubt.

speaker: Teacher (self-made doubter)
question: Who doubts the mother?
premises: mātuḥ svabhāvo yattasyāṃ śaṅkate naiṣa jātucit — of the mother, nature: whoever doubts in her — never this one.
svakṛtatvavaśādeva sarvavitsa hi śaṅkaraḥ — by self-making alone, of the all-knower: for he is the doubter (śaṅkara/śaṅkate pun).
inference: The doubter's doubt is self-made; the all-knower never doubts.

speaker: Teacher (undoubting the self-track)
question: When is there no doubt?
premises: yāvattu śivatā nāsya — as long as Śiva-hood is not in him.
tāvatsvātmānusāriṇīm tāvatīmeva tāmeṣa prasiddhiṃ nābhiśaṅkate — that long, the self-following — that very — her, this certainty — he does not doubt.
inference: Before Śiva-hood, self-following certainty goes undoubted.

speaker: Teacher (esteeming another's)
question: How is another's treated?
premises: anyasyāmabhiśaṅkī syādbhūyastāṃ bahu manyate — in another doubting, she would there much esteem.
evaṃ bhāviśivatvo 'mūṃ prasiddhiṃ manyate dhruvam — thus, in future-Śiva-hood, this certainty is surely esteemed.
inference: Doubt another's, yet esteem it; future Śivahood honors present faith.

speaker: Teacher (one āgama shown)
question: How many āgamas?
premises: eka evāgamaścāyaṃ — one alone āgama — and this.
vibhunā sarvadarśinā darśito yaḥ pravṛtte ca nivṛtte ca pathi sthitaḥ — by the all-seeing Lord shown, standing on the path in activity and cessation.
inference: One āgama, Lord-shown, standing in both ways.

speaker: Teacher (one Śāmbhava means)
question: What single means?
premises: dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu pūrṇāpūrṇādibhedataḥ vicitreṣu phaleṣveka upāyaḥ śāmbhavāgamaḥ — in all aims, through all measures, in various fruits: one means, the Śāmbhava āgama.
inference: One Śāmbhava means for all aims in all measures.

speaker: Teacher (variety, no contradiction)
question: Why no contradiction?
premises: tasminviṣayavaiviktyād vicitraphaladāyini — in that, from subject-variety, in variably-fruit-giving.
citropāyopadeśo 'pi na virodhāvaho bhavet — even the varied-means-teaching brings no contradiction.
inference: Varied patients, varied means — no contradiction.

speaker: Teacher (schools listed)
question: Which schools?
premises: laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ sāṅkhyaṃ yogādi pāñcarātrakam — worldly, Vedic, Sāṅkhya, Yoga and the rest, Pāñcarātra.
bauddhārhatanyāyaśāstraṃ padārthakramatantraṇam — Buddha-Arhat-logic-scriptures, category-sequence-texts.
inference: The curriculum from worldly to logic to categories.

speaker: Teacher (all Brahman-born)
question: Whence all schools?
premises: siddhāntatantraśāktādi sarvaṃ brahmodbhavaṃ — Siddhānta-tantra-Śakti and the rest, all Brahman-born.
yataḥ śrīsvacchandaādiṣu proktaṃ sadyojātādibhedataḥ — for in Svacchanda and the rest so taught, through Sadyoja-differences.
inference: All schools Brahman-born, per Svacchanda's Sadyoja-differences.

speaker: Teacher (Veda initiates too)
question: Does Veda lack saṃskāra?
premises: yathaikatrāpi vedādau tattadāśramagāminaḥ — as in one place even, in Veda and the rest, for going-to-that-that-āśrama.
saṃskārāntaramatrāpi tathā liṅgoddhṛtādikam — another saṃskāra here too; so the liṅga-uddhāra and the rest.
inference: Veda too gives saṃskāra; liṅga-rites likewise here.

speaker: Teacher (grades hold)
question: Do lower rites yield the highest?
premises: yathāca tatra pūrvasminnāśrame nottarāśramāt phalameti — as there, in the earlier āśrama, no fruit comes from the later.
tathā pāñcarātrādau na śivātmatām — so from Pāñcarātra and the rest, no Śiva-nature.
inference: Grades hold: Pāñcarātra rites don't yield Śiva-nature.

speaker: Teacher (one āgama establishes all)
question: What establishes all?
premises: eka evāgamastasmāttatra laukikaśāstrataḥ — one alone āgama — then there, from the worldly scripture.
prabhṛtyāvaiṣṇavādbauddhācchaivātsarvaṃ hi niṣṭhitam — from the beginning — from Vaiṣṇava, Buddhist, Śaiva — all indeed is established.
inference: One āgama establishes all, from worldly to Śaiva.

speaker: Teacher (Trika and Kula named)
question: What is highest?
premises: tasya yattat paraṃ prāpyaṃ dhāma tat trikaśabditam — of it, whatever is the attainable highest state, that is called Trika.
sarvāvibhedānucchedāt tadeva kulamucyate — through non-severance of all-differences, that very is called Kula.
inference: The attainable highest is Trika; undifferentiated, it is Kula.

speaker: Teacher (one life, all scriptures)
question: How is Trika everywhere?
premises: yathordhvādharatābhāksu dehāṅgeṣu vibhediṣu ekaṃ prāṇitamevaṃ syāt — as among high-low-marked divided body-parts there should be one living being.
trikaṃ sarveṣu śāstrataḥ — so Trika, in all, by the scriptures.
inference: As one life in divided limbs, so Trika in all scriptures.

speaker: Teacher (Kālīkula essence)
question: What is the essence?
premises: śrīmatkālīkule coktaṃ — and it is said in the venerable Kālī-kula.
pañcasrotovivarjitam daśāṣṭādaśabhedasya sārametatprakīrtitam — devoid of five streams, of ten-and-eighteen-difference: this essence is declared.
inference: Kālīkula essence beyond five streams, of ten-and-eighteen.

speaker: Teacher (Kula indwells)
question: Where is Kula?
premises: puṣpe gandhastile tailaṃ dehe jīvo jale 'mṛtam — in the flower fragrance, in sesame oil, in the body the soul, in water nectar.
yathā tathaiva śāstrāṇāṃ kulamantaḥ pratiṣṭhitam — as so, of scriptures Kula within is established.
inference: Kula indwells scriptures as fragrance in flowers.

speaker: Teacher (one āgama, varied holders)
question: How one yet varied?
premises: tadeka evāgamo 'yaṃ citraścitre 'dhikāriṇi — that one alone āgama — this, varied, in varied authority-holders.
tathaiva sā prasiddhirhi svayūthyaparayūthyagā — so indeed she, prasiddhi — for, goes in own-flock and other-flock.
inference: One varied āgama for varied holders; one prasiddhi across flocks.

speaker: Teacher (censure none)
question: Blame any school?
premises: sāṅkhyaṃ yogaṃ pāñcarātraṃ vedāṃścaiva na nindayet — Sāṅkhya, Yoga, Pāñcarātra, Vedas — one should not censure.
yataḥ śivodbhavāḥ sarva iti svacchandaśāsane — for all are Śiva-born: thus in the Svacchanda teaching.
inference: Censure no school: all are Śiva-born (Svacchanda).

speaker: Teacher (pieces mislead)
question: Why do people wander?
premises: ekasmādāgamāccaite khaṇḍakhaṇḍā vyapoddhṛtāḥ — from one āgama, and these, plucked out piece by piece.
loke syurāgamāstaiśca jano bhrāmyati mohitaḥ — in the world should be āgamas; and by them the deluded people wander.
inference: Plucked pieces pass as wholes; the deluded wander.

speaker: Teacher (pluralists must rank)
question: What must even pluralists do?
premises: anekāgamapakṣe 'pi vācyā viṣayabheditā — in many-āgama sides too, subject-difference is speakable.
avaśyamūrdhvādharatāsthityā prāmāṇyasiddhaye — necessarily held in high-low-ness, for establishing validity.
inference: Even many-āgama sides must state subjects and rank.

speaker: Teacher (what proves)
question: What makes proof?
premises: anyathā naiva kasyāpi prāmāṇyaṃ siddhyati dhruvam — otherwise no one's validity is ever established, surely.
nityatvamavisaṃvāda iti no mānakāraṇam — permanence-and-noncontradiction, thus, for us are no proof-cause.
inference: Without ranking none are valid; permanence proves nothing.

speaker: Teacher (utterance proves here)
question: What proves in this part?
premises: asminnaṃśe 'pyamuṣyaiva prāmāṇyaṃ syāttathoditeḥ — in this part too, of that very one, validity would be — from that utterance.
anyathāvyākṛtau kḷptāvasatyatve prarocane — otherwise: in non-realization, in fixed non-being, in preference.
inference: Utterance proves here; otherwise counterfactuals.

speaker: Teacher (overreach defeats)
question: What defeats all āgamas?
premises: atiprasaṅga sarvasyāpyāgamasyāpabādhakaḥ — over-implication: of all āgama too, the defeater.
avaśyopetya ityasminmāna āgamanāmani — 'must-reach' — in this, the proof, of the āgama-name: the name proves.
inference: Over-application defeats; the name āgama proves must-reach.

speaker: Teacher (principal limb bears fruit)
question: Where to work?
premises: avaśyopetyamevaitacchāstraniṣṭhānirūpanam — 'must-reach' indeed: this is the account of scriptural endeavor.
pradhāne 'ṅge kṛto yatnaḥ phalavānvastuto yataḥ — in the principal limb effort made is really fruit-bearing.
inference: Endeavor the principal limb: it really bears fruit.

speaker: Teacher (strive Śambhu-impelled)
question: Who should strive?
premises: ato 'smin yatnavān ko 'pi bhavecchambhupracoditaḥ — hence herein anyone striving should be Śambhu-impelled.
tatra tatra ca śāstreṣu nyarūpyata maheśinā — and there, there, in scriptures, was set forth by the Great Lord.
inference: Strive Śambhu-impelled; the Lord set it forth everywhere.

speaker: Teacher (rare fit, told to me)
question: Who is fit, and who told?
premises: etāvatyadhikārī yaḥ sa durlabha iti sphuṭam — at this much the qualified, who, he is hard to find, clearly.
itthaṃ śrīśambhunāthena mamoktaṃ śāstramelanam — thus by venerable Śambhunātha — to me — was told the scripture-union.
inference: Rare the fit; Śambhunātha told me the union: colophon.
